title: High-Speed Recordable Direct Electron Detection Cameras Using SOI-CMOS Technology for Dynamical Observation in Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Temporal resolution in a transmission electron microscope (TEM) is restricted by the read-out time of cameras without an ultra-fast TEM with pulsed electron beams. The read-out speed of the cameras depends on their number of pixels. Since parallel read-outs of whole pixels are difficult, the frame period of commercial cameras for TEMs, which corresponds to temporal resolution, increases with increasing pixel number. In addition, the minimum frame period of the current cameras is the microsecond timescale [1-3]. We cannot get the frame period under sub-microseconds using the current cameras. To overcome the limitation, we have developed a novel direct electron detection camera based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) CMOS technology, named the Silicon-on-insulator for Time-Resolved Imaging in Electron Microscopy (STRIEM) [4], which is capable of sub-microsecond imaging. In the present paper, we will report the development status of the STRIEM cameras and their demonstration results.
